conviction_note: Strong evidence of a likely beat on the quarter: the company has beaten consensus in 8 of 8 quarters, and Q2 revenue came in $0.2bn above the top of its own guide. The stock has already fallen 24% in 20 days with no company-specific negative news, and short interest is low. Against that: the market sold the January and April beats by 13-14%, the move turns on 2027/2028 investor-day targets whose sell-side bar I could not source, and the AI-financing scare (OpenAI run-rate, TSMC caution on 2027) is a live proxy negative. The option market pays for downside (skew +8.3). So p_up is only 53, giving (2*0.53-1)*12.5 = +0.75. That is close to the findings' sum of +0.6, because both measurements took the same caveats once.
bar: Q3 2026 company guide: revenue $5.25-5.55bn, adj EPS $2.88-3.08 (Q2 release, https://corporate.celestica.com/node/17606, 2026-07-27). Consensus at or just above the guide midpoint, from three agreeing sources: $2.94 / $5.39bn (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-10-26-celestica-inc-stock/), $2.94 / $5.37bn (Investing.com, 2026-10-22), $2.99 / $5.44bn (Investing.com preview, 2026-10-26). FY2026 company outlook: ~$20.5bn revenue, adj EPS $11.30. 2027: the company says only that revenue growth will accelerate beyond 2026's 65% (so >~$33.8bn) and EPS growth will outpace revenue. The sell-side 2027/2028 bar the investor day will be judged against is UNSOURCED (one aggregator implies 2027 EPS ~$18.5), so the guidance finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest ~3.3m shares, ~2.8% of float, days to cover ~1.0 (Equibles snapshot dated 2026-08-20, https://equibles.com/stocks/cls/shortinterest). Older MarketBeat pages show 3.4-5.2% of float with 1-1.7 days to cover. No October FINRA figure found. Not a crowded short. Skew: 25d put minus call = +8.26 vol points, put/call OI 1.34, so downside is paid for. Event-implied move 11.37% (straddle 12.67%, ATM IV 136%). Tape: -10.0% over 5 days, -24.2% over 20 days, -42.8% from the 52-week high, +8.3% off the 52-week low. On Oct 22 the stock fell ~10-11.5% in a sector-wide AI selloff with no company news (Quiver, Investing.com). Insiders: 150 sales and 0 buys in 6 months; CEO 345,949 shares (~$130.7m) under a 10b5-1 plan. Q2 13F flows: Viking exited (-1.65m shares), JPM +3.9m, D.E. Shaw +1.8m.

findings.finding: Celestica has beaten its own revenue guide by a wide margin each quarter. Q2 2026 revenue was $4.70bn against a $4.2-4.5bn guide (4.4% above the top) and a $4.30bn consensus, with adj EPS $2.54 against $2.29, and it has beaten EPS consensus in 8 of 8 quarters. The Q3 consensus of $5.37-5.44bn / $2.94-2.99 sits at the guide midpoint ($5.40bn / $2.98). The Q2 call said component availability, not demand, is the binding constraint. A repeat of the Q2 pattern implies roughly $5.6-5.8bn of revenue, about 4-6% above the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats were sold twice and bought twice. Jan 2026 (Q4 beat): -13.1%. Apr 2026 (Q1 beat plus FY raise to $19bn): -14.4%. Jul 2026 (Q2 beat above the guide top, FY raised to $20.5bn): +10.0%. Oct 2025 (beat plus early 2026 outlook): +8.2%. So a beat alone does not decide the sign.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits at the guide midpoint, not near the top or above it, even though the last quarter came in above the top. If the market expected a repeat beat, published consensus would sit at about $5.6bn. Some buy-side whisper is likely above consensus (one SA preview, 2026-10-23, models $5.57bn / $3.10), so part of this is probably in the price.
findings.independence: Same pattern in the company's Q2 release (https://corporate.celestica.com/node/17606: 'Q2 2026 revenue and adjusted EPS above the high end of our guidance ranges'). Supplier read: TSMC Q3 revenue above the top of its guide, with demand still exceeding supply (https://www.crnasia.com/news/2026/components-and-peripherals/tsmc-third-quarter-revenue-tops-guidance-as-ceo-says-ai-dema, 2026-10-15).

findings.finding: The Q3 print comes with the 2026 Investor & Analyst Day (Oct 27, 08:00 ET), inside the window. Multi-year targets will be reset there. The company has already committed to 2027 revenue growth above 2026's 65% (implying more than ~$33.8bn on the $20.5bn FY26 outlook), with EPS growth outpacing revenue. Counterparties who have spoken since July point the same way. Broadcom (Sept 3) guided AI revenue of $115bn in FY27 and $230bn in FY28, about double each year; Celestica builds Broadcom-based switches and the OpenAI/Broadcom XPU racks. Jabil (Sept 30) guided FY27 AI revenue +54% and cloud/data-center +52%. Celestica's own 424B5 (Aug 6) lists new wins: a 1.6T scale-up switch for AMD Helios and a 1.6T co-packaged-optics program with a hyperscaler.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Oct 2025, the last time a forward year was first framed at Q3: +8.2%. Jul 2026, FY raise plus 2027 acceleration language: +10.0%. Apr 2026, FY raise judged not big enough: -14.4%. Guidance is the line this stock moves on, in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is 43% below its high and fell 24% in 20 days without company news, while consensus price targets (~$450-471) have not moved. That suggests the price, not the published estimates, is discounting a 2027 that disappoints. If the market were pricing the Broadcom/Jabil trajectory, the stock would not be trading at the price of the August $310 offering minus 13%. Caveat, applied once in the size: the sell-side 2027/2028 bar is unsourced, so a 2027 number at 'just above 65%' could land as a disappointment.
findings.independence: Broadcom FY27/FY28 AI targets: https://pulse2.com/broadcom-q3-fiscal-2026-revenue-jumps-86-to-29-6-billion-as-ai-semiconductor-revenue-reaches-16-7-billion/ (2026-09-03). Jabil FY27 guide: https://www.itiger.com/news/1118646763 (2026-09-30). Celestica 424B5 program wins: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1030894/000110465926091994/tm2621135d3_424b5.htm (2026-08-06). These are three different issuers; the Celestica 2027 language and the 424B5 are both company documents.

findings.finding: The stock goes into the print -24.2% over 20 days, -10.0% over 5 days and -42.8% from its 52-week high. The Oct 22 fall of ~10-11.5% came with 'no fresh negative company announcement' (Quiver) and was described as pre-earnings de-risking in a sector-wide AI selloff. Short interest is low (~2.8% of float, ~1 day to cover), so the decline is longs reducing, not shorts building.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jul 2026: the stock had fallen 8.9% on 2026-07-24, just before the print, and then rose +10.0% on a beat and raise. Jan and Apr 2026 prints came after run-ups and were sold (-13.1%, -14.4%).
findings.why_not_priced: This finding goes against the +8.3 put skew. Why the option market may be wrong about this print: the puts are being bought by long holders hedging after a 24% slide, not as an informed short (short interest ~1 day to cover), and the slide came from sector beta rather than Celestica news. A guide that merely confirms the existing 2027 framing therefore has room to recover. If de-risking had not happened, the stock would sit near the $357 it traded at on 2026-09-28. Sized small because the skew is a real directional statement.
findings.independence: Investing.com, 2026-10-22, attributes the drop to pre-earnings risk reduction and sector sentiment (https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-celestica-stock-tumbling-today-93CH-4967215). Short interest: https://equibles.com/stocks/cls/shortinterest (2026-08-20).

findings.finding: OpenAI demand risk. On Oct 8 the FT reported OpenAI's annualised revenue run-rate approaching ~$50bn against ~$70bn the market had assumed, and on Oct 12 the CEOs of Broadcom and Intel named access to capital and financing costs as possible constraints on AI build-out. Celestica's OpenAI/Broadcom custom-rack program, with initial deliveries guided for late 2026, is a named growth leg in its 2027 acceleration. Investor-day questions on the size and timing of this program are likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on a single customer's financing. The stock fell with the sector on these headlines in October (20-day -24%).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the sector selloff is the market's reaction to this. The unpriced part is company-specific. If management softens OpenAI rack timing or volume at the investor day, it lands directly on the 2027 targets. Net of the rest of the company: three customers are ~63% of revenue, Google-led networking and compute is the bulk of CCS, and AMD Helios is separate, so OpenAI is one leg, not the 2027 number.
findings.independence: Proxy; Celestica has not commented. Broadcom's Sept call said Jalapeno shipments for OpenAI continue (https://pulse2.com/broadcom-q3-fiscal-2026-revenue-jumps-86-to-29-6-billion-as-ai-semiconductor-revenue-reaches-16-7-billion/), which cuts against it, so the finding is sized small.

findings.finding: On TSMC's Oct 15 Q3 call, the CFO said the company is being 'prudent in our business planning going into 2027' and gave no 2027 capex guidance, while also raising 2026 USD growth to ~44% and saying AI demand exceeds supply. This is a cautious 2027 tone from the most upstream supplier, into an investor day whose whole thesis is 2027 acceleration.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it was public on Oct 15 and the stock has fallen since. Kept as a small proxy because a 2027 hedge from TSMC raises the odds that sell-side 2027 numbers for the EMS chain are already trimmed, or that Celestica guides conservatively.
findings.independence: Proxy. The same TSMC call is the positive source in finding 1 (demand above supply), so the two readings share one document: TSMC is net mixed.

findings.finding: The $3bn equity raise (9.68m shares at $310, closed ~Aug 7-12) funds working capital and capex for hyperscaler demand. The 424B5 cites LTM gross capex of $625m, the AMD Helios 1.6T switch and a 1.6T CPO hyperscaler win, and says demand growth 'has required' a greater focus on capacity and working capital. On what the money buys, the answer is a ramp. The raise also removes balance-sheet questions at the investor day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell after the raise (Benzinga, Aug 2026). Dilution of about 8% is already in the share count.
findings.why_not_priced: The dilution is priced. The use of proceeds, capacity behind confirmed programs, gets confirmed only when capex and working capital show in the Q3 cash flow and 2027 targets. Small.
findings.independence: Company press release on the offering (https://corporate.celestica.com/node/17646, 2026-08-05). Same issuer, so not independent of the 424B5.

findings.finding: CFO transition right before the investor day. From Oct 1, CFO Mandeep Chawla moved to a newly created Group President, Global Markets role and Todd Ankenmann became CFO (8-K items 5.02, 2026-09-11). This Q3 print and the multi-year targets are the new CFO's first. Separately, CCS segment president Jason Phillips retired in July (replaced by Steven Dorwart).
findings.why_not_priced: Public for six weeks, and it reads as a promotion, not a departure. The only residual is the risk that a new CFO sets the multi-year targets conservatively.

findings.finding: Steady insider selling into the print: 150 open-market sales and 0 buys in 6 months. CEO Robert Mionis sold 345,949 shares (~$130.7m) under a 10b5-1 plan, with the latest Form 4s filed 2026-09-24 and 2026-10-01. The CFO sold 34,000 shares (~$13.1m).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measurable. The sales were under a plan and well publicised.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. These are 10b5-1 sales that were cited in previews as a sentiment weight. Kept small because the absence of any insider buying after a 43% drawdown says management is not signalling.
findings.independence: EDGAR filing index shows Form 4s dated 2026-09-24 and 2026-10-01 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001030894&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40). Investing.com, 2026-10-22, cites 243,067 shares / $89.2m sold in 90 days.

baseline_tension: Cuts against the skew: puts are bid at +8.3 and the 20-day run-up is -24%. I lean slightly long because the de-rating came from sector beta with no company news and short interest is low, but the January and April beats were sold, so p_up is held at 53.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a reaction): reported-quarter beat finding cut from +1.0 to +0.7, because two of the last four beats were sold by 13-14%.
Rule 6 (bar): the Q3 bar is sourced (company guide plus three agreeing estimates), but the 2027/2028 investor-day bar is unsourced, so the guidance finding is capped from +1.5 to +1.0.

Rule 7 (positioning): the positioning long goes against +8.3 skew, so it was cut from +1.0 to +0.7 with an explicit reason; short interest was checked (~2.8% of float, ~1 day to cover), so the negatives were not shrunk for squeeze risk.
Rule 4 (financing): the equity raise funds a corroborated ramp, so the sign stays positive, trimmed to +0.2 because it is priced.
Rule 5 (proxies): OpenAI and TSMC proxies left small, as drafted, and the shared TSMC document is noted in independence.

Rule 3 / scaled number: p_up moved from 55 to 53 for the skew and sold-beat caveats, so expected_move goes from +1.25 to +0.75; abs_move_pct stays at 12.5 (implied 11.4, median history 13.1, plus investor day).
